what_happened: Task 786's premise -- four wired evidence probes with independent source-level compile failures needing per-probe repair/restatement/retirement -- is falsified by re-measurement. All four compile today unchanged since 2026-10-03, and 'bash scripts/check-evidence-probes.sh' prints 'PASS all 33 wired probe(s) compile'. The archived phase-4 gate log from the originating run shows all four errors were 'object file ... does not exist' missing-.olean I/O errors on four distinct FormalSystem import-closure tail modules (Metalogic, MainResults, Examples.Walkthrough, Examples), on four CONSECUTIVE WIRED entries (9-12 of 33), with those oleans' mtimes falling inside the gate's own run window. Root cause is a .lake read/write race: check-evidence-probes.sh calls bare 'lake env lean' 33 times without taking the shared .lake/build-guard.lock that check-module-invariants.sh and lake-build-guard.sh both take.

The originating run's full gate output, including the per-probe error text the task description lacked, survived in the prior session's scratchpad (p4-gate.log) and subagent transcript. Reading those turned an open four-way diagnosis into a single-cause determination in minutes and avoided four speculative probe rewrites.

Planning surfaced a second consumer of the file under edit that the research report did not name: scripts/generate-decidability-inventory.sh regex-parses check-evidence-probes.sh's WIRED/WIRED_REPO array anchors behind an anti-silence guard and derives ALL_PASS/SOME_FAIL from its exit status. This constrained the lock block's insertion point (after both arrays, never between the comment table and WIRED=() and set Phase 2's verification tier to interface with that script named as the enumerated dependent check.

Phase 2's verification criterion asked for 'no diff against the committed baseline' from scripts/generate-decidability-inventory.sh --diff, but that script reports pre-existing drift (+/- REFUTED lines) against an archived, curated review baseline and still exits 0. Since this task touches no WIRED/WIRED_REPO array line, SRC2's input is byte-identical to the pre-edit file, so the drift is pre-existing by construction. Verified the satisfiable criterion instead: exit 0, no FAIL SRC2 anti-silence line, arrays parsed as 32 WIRED + 1 WIRED_REPO = 33.

Phase 3's prescribed locator 'grep -n "not wired into CI"' returns no hit: the stale claim is line-wrapped in the source as '...is not wired into' / '# CI.'. Followed the phase's own stop-and-re-read instruction and located the sentence by its wrapped two-line text rather than by the line number the record quoted.
